# Getting started

## This template

Paillasse is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org) theme for reveal.js slides: 16:9 slides, a clean left-aligned layout, and a colour palette inspired by the CNRS visual identity.

- Write your slides in this file, then run `quarto preview` or `quarto render`.
- Settings live in the YAML header at the top: title, authors, logos, footer, language.
- `##` headings start a new slide. `#` headings create a **section divider**, like the previous slide.

## Logos

Title-slide logos are listed under `title-logos` in the YAML header:

```yaml
title-logos:
  - src: logos/CNRS.png
    alt: CNRS
  - src: logos/my-lab.png
    alt: My lab
```

To show a small logo on every content slide, add `logo: logos/my-lab.png`. It is hidden on the title slide and on section dividers. `footer: "..."` adds text at the bottom of each slide.

# Writing slides

## Text and lists

Markdown gives you **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [links](https://quarto.org) and footnotes[^1].

- Leave an empty line before a list, otherwise it joins the paragraph above.
- Indent an item by two spaces to nest it:
  - nested items get an arrow,
  - in the palette's cyan.

1. Numbered lists use the same colour.
2. A second item.

[^1]: Footnotes go at the bottom of the slide.

## Colours

Coloured text with `.fg-*`: [blue]{.fg-blue}, [red]{.fg-red}, [purple]{.fg-purple}.

Highlights with `.hl-*`: [blue]{.hl-blue} [cyan]{.hl-cyan} [orange]{.hl-orange} [green]{.hl-green} [purple]{.hl-purple} [red]{.hl-red} [yellow]{.hl-yellow}

::: {.callout-tip}
Cyan, orange, green and yellow are too light for text on a white background, especially on a projector: use them for highlights, figures and shapes.
:::

In inline SVG, `class="fg-orange"` sets fill and stroke; in any CSS, `var(--pal-orange)` gives the colour. `.alert` is kept as a shortcut for `.hl-red`.

## Two columns

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Left

- Columns are set with `.columns` and `.column` divs.
- Widths are in percent.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Right

- Put text, a figure or code in each column.
- Widths should add up to 100%.
:::
::::

## Equations

Inline maths goes between single dollars: a signal $x[n]$ of length $N$.

Display maths goes between double dollars. Add a label after the closing `$$` to number the equation:

$$
X[k] = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] \, e^{-2 i \pi k n / N}, \qquad k = 0, \dots, N-1
$$ {#eq-dft}

Then refer to it in the text: @eq-dft defines the discrete Fourier transform.

## Code and figures

To give figures the same colours as the slides, set the palette once in Python:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from cycler import cycler

palette = ["#003a70", "#00a3e0", "#f39200", "#009640",
           "#662483", "#e1000f", "#f2c500"]
plt.rcParams["axes.prop_cycle"] = cycler(color=palette)
```

In R, use `scale_colour_manual(values = palette)` with the same colours.

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
Notes use the primary blue.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Important points use the accent red.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Warnings use yellow. Read more in the [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/callouts.html).
:::

# Presenting

## Step by step

Content can appear one piece at a time.

. . .

- Use `. . .` on its own line to pause,

. . .

- or wrap a list in `::: incremental` to reveal it item by item.

## Section dividers

Every `#` heading becomes a divider slide with a coloured background.

- Skip it for one section with `# Title {.no-divider}`.
- Turn dividers off with `section-divider: false` in the YAML header.
- Change their colour with `section-divider-color: "#662483"`.

## PDF export

Open the slides in Chrome, Edge or another Chromium-based browser and press `E`: the slides switch to a print layout, one page per slide.

Then print to PDF. In the print dialog, set the margins to **None** so that each slide fills its page.

Press `E` again to return to the normal view.
